- /opt/nxeon/components/customer/CloudflareIntegration.tsx (108)

Hunt for exactly these four defect classes. Report each with absolute file path:line and one sentence on what a customer experiences:

1. UNCONTROLLED FORM INPUTS. React 19 RESETS an uncontrolled field on every `<form action={fn}>` submit (a form whose `action` prop is a server action or a `useActionState` dispatch). Any `<input>`/`<textarea>`/`<select>` inside such a form with no `value={}`/`checked={}` prop loses its content on a rejected submit — e.g. a DNS record value or an EPP auth code retyped from scratch. Check every input/textarea/select and state which submit mechanism its form uses (form action= / onSubmit / onClick).

2. DISPLAYED != CHARGED. Any rendered price derived locally rather than taken from the shared pricing source the server actually charges through. For domains the price comes from lib/namecheap.ts TLD_PRICES plus an admin markup setting — check that any price shown to the customer (search results, register wizard, renewal, transfer) comes from the same server-side computation the charge uses, not from a locally re-derived markup or a hardcoded number. This repo has shipped "$8.99 shown / $6.29 charged" and an admin panel showing 0% markup while customers were charged 25%.

3. A CONTROL THAT REPORTS AN OUTCOME IT DID NOT VERIFY. A success toast on a fire-and-forget call; an optimistic state update never reconciled; a green check/badge derived from "we asked" rather than "it happened". A KNOWN instance to verify is still true: the domain checklist's "WHOIS privacy on" green tick — `setWhoisPrivacy` in lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts reportedly writes a local boolean and never contacts the registrar, while app/dashboard/domains/[id]/page.tsx renders a green tick for it. Read those and confirm or refute. Also check DNS record writes, nameserver changes, Cloudflare connect, and transfer status.

4. DEAD ENDS. A disabled button with no explanation of what would enable it; an empty state that names a UI which is not rendered; an error that says what went wrong but not how to fix it; a destructive action (delete DNS record, delete domain, change nameservers, cancel transfer) with no confirmation or one that does not state the real consequence; a form that loses long free text.

ALSO check: horizontal overflow at a 390px viewport (grid tracks whose children lack min-w-0 are the known cause in this repo, not tables — long unbreakable strings like DNS values and auth codes set a min-content floor), keyboard focus visibility, and Escape handling plus accessible names on any modal/drawer.

DO NOT modify any file. DO NOT run npm build. Read-only investigation. You MAY read lib/ files to trace what a control actually does.

Report as a plain list. Give every listed file a verdict line (CLEAN / defects found) — account for all 14. Be precise with line numbers, and distinguish what you verified by reading from what you infer.
